Also HAZARD 2 R-value-only (R-30 -> band null + spokenRValue 30), HAZARD 4-style enum paraphrase "some insulation but really thin" -> wallInsulated=poorly (not yes), duct insulation "no insulation ... bare metal" -> none, and "very leaky". Partial model number G-something -> null.

notes.heatingFuel: THE silent-drop trap. Equipment is unambiguous (furnace) but the auditor explicitly says he never checked the fuel and won't guess. Correct = null with span. Any fuel value here (natural_gas is the tempting default for a furnace) is a hallucination of exactly the kind the fuel axis is meant to expose. This is the highest-weight null in the corpus for hazard 1.
notes.wallInsulated: 3-state paraphrase: "some insulation but it's really thin, patchy" -> poorly, NOT yes. Collapsing poorly->yes is the specific enum-mapping error README section 4 flags.
notes.atticInsulationDepthIn: R-value only (R-30, explicitly eyeballed, "didn't measure the depth") -> band null. Converting R-30 to a depth band is the forbidden conversion.
notes.heatingModelNumber: "G-something" is a non-committal partial, not a model number -> null. "G" alone is not a usable value.
notes.coolingEquipmentType: central_ac_standalone_ducts: the AC is explicitly its own attic ductwork, separate from the furnace. Genuinely standalone, unlike the shared-duct case in transcript 13.
notes._general: No safety, DHW, blower door, or windows discussed -> all null. "a couple inches of old batt" is a wall-cavity observation supporting poorly, not an attic depth.
